# Gramless — Consolidated Documentation (llms-full.txt)

> Zero-dependency, transactional Telegram framework for Telegram Serverless (TGCloud), edge V8 isolates (Cloudflare Workers, Vercel), and Node.js.
> Source repository: https://github.com/sidwiskers/gramless
> Online documentation: https://sidwiskers.github.io/gramless/

---



<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: guide/what-is-gramless.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# What is Gramless?

**Gramless** is a zero-dependency Telegram bot framework built for **Telegram Serverless (TGCloud)**, Cloudflare Workers, and traditional Node.js servers.

It provides pre-compiled route dispatching, transactional SQLite sessions with automatic rollback, composable filters, Bot API helpers, Mini App RPC endpoints, and an in-memory testing lab.

---

## Background & Rationale

Traditional Node.js bot libraries (such as grammY and Telegraf) were designed for long-running servers with persistent processes and local `node_modules` installations.

In serverless V8 environments such as TGCloud:
1. **No Runtime Package Manager:** TGCloud isolates execute pure JavaScript modules directly and do not support `node_modules` at runtime.
2. **Server Assumptions:** Traditional frameworks rely on long-polling loops or local HTTP server bindings that are incompatible with isolated serverless handlers.
3. **Session Consistency:** Storing state in process memory or uncoordinated database writes can lead to lost updates when concurrent webhooks execute across multiple isolates.

Gramless addresses these constraints by compiling routing tables at startup, executing with zero external runtime dependencies, and managing state through atomic SQLite transactions.

---

## Comparison

| Feature | Traditional Frameworks | Gramless |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Runtime Dependencies** | 15–40 packages | **0 packages** |
| **Command Lookup (1,000 routes)** | Linear regex scan | **$O(1)$ Hash Map (2.25 µs)** |
| **Callback Query Dispatch** | Linear search | **$O(1)$ Hash Map & Prefix Index (0.92 µs)** |
| **Session Persistence** | In-memory cache or external DB | **ACID SQLite with automatic rollback** |
| **Mini App Endpoints** | External web server | **Built-in `createEndpoint` + `v` validator** |
| **Offline Testing** | Requires live bot token or mocks | **In-memory test lab (`gramless/testkit`)** |
| **Supported Runtimes** | Node.js servers | **TGCloud, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel, Node.js** |

---

<!-- SECTION: guide/getting-started.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Quickstart Guide

Get up and running with **Gramless** on Telegram Serverless in under 2 minutes.

---

## 1. Quick Scaffolding (Recommended)

Scaffold a complete project interactively in seconds:

::: code-group
```bash [npm]
npm create gramless@latest
```
```bash [pnpm]
pnpm create gramless
```
```bash [yarn]
yarn create gramless
```
```bash [bun]
bun create gramless
```
:::

Select your desired runtime (*TGCloud Serverless*, *Cloudflare Workers*, *Node.js Polling*, or *Fullstack Mini App*), and the directory structure, configuration, and starter code are generated automatically.

---

## 2. Manual Installation

Or install Gramless directly into an existing project:

::: code-group
```bash [npm]
npm install gramless
```
```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add gramless
```
```bash [yarn]
yarn add gramless
```
:::

---

## 2. Project Directory Structure

TGCloud projects use a clean convention where backend code lives inside `tgcloud/`:

```text
my-tgcloud-bot/
├── tgcloud/
│   ├── handlers/
│   │   ├── message.js          # Receives text, commands, and media
│   │   └── callback_query.js   # Receives inline keyboard button clicks
│   └── lib/
│       └── bot.js              # Central bot routing definition
├── package.json
└── tgcloud.jsonc
```

---

## 3. Creating the Bot (`tgcloud/lib/bot.js`)

Define your commands and interactive button handlers:

```javascript
import { createBot } from 'gramless';

export const bot = createBot();

bot.command('start', async (ctx) => {
  await ctx.chatAction('typing');

  await ctx.reply(`Welcome <b>${ctx.from?.first_name || 'User'}</b>!`, {
    parse_mode: 'HTML',
    buttons: [
      [{ text: 'Ping isolate', data: 'action:ping' }],
    ],
  });
});

bot.action('action:ping', async (ctx) => {
  await ctx.answer({ text: 'Pong received' });
  await ctx.edit('<b>Pong</b>. Isolate responsive.', {
    parse_mode: 'HTML',
  });
});
```

---

## 4. Re-exporting Handlers (`tgcloud/handlers/message.js`)

In TGCloud, update handlers are discrete entry files. Re-export `bot.handler()` from each handler file:

```javascript
import { bot } from '../lib/bot.js';

export default bot.handler();
```

Do the same for `tgcloud/handlers/callback_query.js`:

```javascript
import { bot } from '../lib/bot.js';

export default bot.handler();
```

---

## 5. Deploying to TGCloud

Authenticate and deploy with the official `@tgcloud/cli`:

```bash
# Preview changes
tgcloud diff

# Deploy to global edge isolates
tgcloud push
```

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: guide/architecture.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# TGCloud Architecture & Mental Model

Understanding the execution lifecycle of **Telegram Serverless** and how **Gramless** optimizes performance within V8 isolates.

---

## The V8 Isolate Lifecycle

Unlike a traditional Node.js server that runs continuously on a single machine, Telegram Serverless runs discrete **V8 isolates** near the user:

```text
Incoming Telegram Update (Webhook)
               │
               ▼
   [TGCloud Edge Dispatcher]
               │
    ┌──────────┴──────────┐
    ▼                     ▼
handlers/message.js   handlers/callback_query.js
    │                     │
    └──────────┬──────────┘
               │
               ▼
       [bot.handler()]
               │
         Gramless Engine:
         • $O(1)$ Hash Route Dispatch
         • ACID Session Staging
         • Composable Filter Guards
               │
               ▼
       Handler Execution
               │
         (On Success)
               ▼
  [Commit SQLite State & Reply]
```

### Key Serverless Principles

1. **No Tokens in Code:** The runtime injects the authenticated API proxy automatically via `import { api } from 'sdk'`. You never commit bot tokens to repository configs.
2. **No Persistent Event Loops:** Never invoke `bot.start()` or `bot.launch()`. Export `bot.handler()`.
3. **Atomic SQLite:** All database persistence runs via built-in SQLite (`sdk/db`) with zero network round-trip overhead.

---

## Important Runtime Constraints

- **Relative Imports Require Extensions:** Always write `import { bot } from './lib/bot.js'`. Omitting `.js` will cause module resolution errors in production.
- **Async Database Calls:** Every query in `sdk/db` must be awaited (`await db.select()...run()`).
- **No Foreign Key Declarations:** `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF`. Do not use `.references()`.
- **Always Answer Callback Queries:** Call `await ctx.answer()` inside button handlers to dismiss loading feedback.

---

## Deploying to TGCloud V8 Isolates

Telegram Serverless isolates execute JavaScript directly from `tgcloud/` without an npm runtime. You can deploy Gramless using either of two workflows:

### 1. Zero-Build Vendoring (Recommended for pure serverless)
Vendor Gramless directly into your project's `tgcloud/lib/`:
```bash
npx gramless vendor
```
Then import natively with relative paths:
```javascript
import { createBot, Filter, session } from '../lib/gramless.js';
```

### 2. Bundled Workflow
If using npm package specifiers (`import { createBot } from 'gramless'`), use a bundler (e.g., `esbuild` or `vite`) to produce flat output files in `tgcloud/` prior to running `tgcloud push`.

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: guide/routing.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Routing & Middleware

Gramless features a compiled, constant-time router designed for zero array allocations on the hot execution path.

---

## Command Routing ($O(1)$)

Commands are registered on the bot instance and resolved via a pre-compiled `Map`:

```javascript
bot.command('start', async (ctx) => {
  await ctx.reply('Bot started!');
});

// Accessing command arguments
bot.command('kick', async (ctx) => {
  // e.g. /kick @spammer 10m
  console.log('Payload:', ctx.payload); // "@spammer 10m"
  console.log('Args:', ctx.args);       // ["@spammer", "10m"]
});
```

### Multiline & Group Chat Parsing
- Automatically handles multiline arguments (`/cmd\nline1\tline2`).
- Filters out commands directed at other bots in group chats (e.g. `/start@other_bot` is ignored if `username` is configured).

---

## Callback Query Routing

Inline keyboard button presses can be matched using exact strings, prefixes, or regular expressions:

```javascript
// 1. Exact string matching (O(1) Map lookup):
bot.action('settings:view', async (ctx) => {
  await ctx.answer();
});

// 2. Prefix matching (ordered by descending prefix length):
bot.action('user:page:', async (ctx) => {
  const page = ctx.callbackData.replace('user:page:', '');
  await ctx.answer();
});

// 3. Regular Expression matching:
bot.action(/^order:(\d+):cancel$/, async (ctx) => {
  const orderId = ctx.match[1];
  await ctx.answer(`Order #${orderId} cancelled`);
});
```

---

## HTML Widget Query Routing (Bot API 10.4)

Queries sent from interactive HTML widgets are routed via `bot.widgetQuery(trigger, ...)` or shorthand `bot.widget(trigger, ...)`:

```javascript
// 1. Exact data match:
bot.widget('poll:vote:option_a', async (ctx) => {
  await ctx.answerWidgetQuery('{"status": "recorded"}');
  await ctx.editMessageWidgetData({ data: 'poll_state:voted' });
});

// 2. Length-sorted prefix match:
bot.widgetQuery('cart:', async (ctx) => {
  await ctx.answerWidgetQuery('{"cart_updated": true}');
});

// 3. Regular Expression match:
bot.widgetQuery(/^candidate:(\w+)$/, async (ctx) => {
  const candidate = ctx.match[1];
  await ctx.answerWidgetQuery(`{"selected": "${candidate}"}`);
});

// 4. Shared widget updates:
bot.on('shared_widget_query', async (ctx) => {
  await ctx.answerWidgetQuery('{"shared": true}');
});
```

---

## Middleware Pipeline

Gramless supports Onion-model middleware. Middlewares are compiled at registration time into a single executable closure chain:

```javascript
// Global logging middleware
bot.use(async (ctx, next) => {
  const start = Date.now();
  await next();
  console.log(`Update processed in ${Date.now() - start}ms`);
});

// Authentication middleware
bot.use(async (ctx, next) => {
  if (ctx.userId === BANNED_USER_ID) return;
  return next();
});
```

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: guide/context.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Context & Bot API Facade

`GramlessContext` is the ergonomic interface passed to every route handler and middleware. It wraps the entire Telegram Bot API, automatically inferring identifiers like `chat_id` and `message_id`.

---

## High-Level Message Helpers

```javascript
// Send text with keyboard buttons
await ctx.reply('Hello!', {
  parse_mode: 'HTML',
  buttons: [
    [{ text: 'Visit Website', url: 'https://tgcloud.ai' }],
    [{ text: 'Action', data: 'action:do' }],
  ],
});

// Edit existing message or reply markup
await ctx.edit('Updated content');
await ctx.editCaption('New caption');
await ctx.editKeyboard([[{ text: 'Refreshed', data: 'noop' }]]);

// Pinning, forwarding, and deleting
await ctx.pin();
await ctx.unpin();
await ctx.delete();
await ctx.forward(targetChatId);
await ctx.copy(targetChatId);
```

---

## Media & Engagement Methods

```javascript
// Media
await ctx.sendPhoto(fileId, { caption: 'Landscape' });
await ctx.sendVideo(fileId);
await ctx.sendVoice(fileId);
await ctx.sendDocument(fileId);
await ctx.sendAnimation(gifId);

// Engagement
await ctx.chatAction('typing');
await ctx.sendPoll('Poll Question', ['Option A', 'Option B']);
await ctx.sendDice('🎯');
```

---

## Interactive HTML Widgets & Ephemeral Replies (Bot API 10.4)

```javascript
// 1. Send an interactive HTML widget (1-32,768 bytes, private chats):
await ctx.sendWidget('<div><h3>Vote 2026</h3><button>Candidate A</button></div>', {
  widget_id: 'voting_widget',
  cache_time: 300,
});

// 2. Re-send a shared widget:
await ctx.sendSharedWidget('shared_leaderboard_xyz');

// 3. Ephemeral callback reply without passing chat_id:
await ctx.replyEphemeral('This reply is only visible to you!');

// 4. Quoting rich messages:
await ctx.reply('Quoting rich block', {
  quote_rich_texts: true,
  quote: 'Target quote',
});
```

---

## Execution Budget & Transactional Checkpointing

```javascript
// Inspect time remaining before platform isolate termination:
console.log(`Remaining budget: ${ctx.remainingMs()}ms`);

if (ctx.hasTimeFor(1500)) {
  // Commit intermediate session state to SQLite immediately:
  await ctx.checkpoint();
}
```

---

## Direct API Access (`ctx.call`)

Any method supported by the Telegram Bot API can be called directly:

```javascript
await ctx.call('sendPaidMedia', {
  chat_id: ctx.chatId,
  star_count: 10,
  media: [...],
});
```

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: guide/filters.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Composable Functional Filters

Gramless provides pure functional filters (`Filter`) to route and guard handlers without reflection or bloated regex overhead.

---

## Logical Combinators

Compose complex conditions cleanly:

```javascript
import { Filter } from 'gramless';

// 1. Filter.all (Logical AND)
const adminGroupPhoto = Filter.all(
  Filter.group,
  Filter.fromUsers(123456, 789012),
  Filter.hasPhoto
);

bot.on(adminGroupPhoto, async (ctx) => {
  await ctx.reply('Admin photo received in group.');
});

// 2. Filter.any (Logical OR)
const voiceOrAudio = Filter.any(Filter.hasVoice, Filter.hasAudio);

// 3. Filter.not (Logical NOT)
const nonBotMessage = Filter.not(Filter.isBot);
```

---

## Standard Predicates

| Predicate | Condition |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Filter.private` | `ctx.chatType === 'private'` |
| `Filter.group` | `ctx.chatType === 'group' \|\| ctx.chatType === 'supergroup'` |
| `Filter.channel` | `ctx.chatType === 'channel'` |
| `Filter.hasText` | Update contains non-empty text |
| `Filter.hasPhoto` | Update contains photos |
| `Filter.hasVideo` | Update contains videos |
| `Filter.hasDocument` | Update contains documents |
| `Filter.hasVoice` | Update contains voice notes |
| `Filter.hasLocation` | Update contains GPS coordinates |
| `Filter.fromUsers(...ids)` | Author matches one of the specified user IDs |
| `Filter.regex(pattern)` | Message text matches regular expression |

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: guide/sessions.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# ACID Sessions & Concurrency

Gramless includes a transactional session engine that guarantees state consistency and automatic error rollback across serverless V8 isolate executions.

---

## Transactional Rollback

In standard frameworks, mutating session state immediately mutates external storage. If an external API call fails halfway through the handler, your database is corrupted with dirty data.

In Gramless, mutations to `ctx.session` are held in an isolated working copy:
- **On Handler Success:** The new state is atomically committed to SQLite (`sdk/db`).
- **On Handler Error or Panic:** The working copy is discarded. **Zero changes are committed to SQLite.**

```javascript
import { createBot, session, TgCloudSessionStore } from 'gramless';
import { db } from 'sdk';
import { eq } from 'sdk/db';
import { sessions } from '../schema.js';

const bot = createBot();

bot.use(session({
  store: new TgCloudSessionStore({ db, table: sessions, eq }),
  initial: () => ({ balance: 100 }),
}));

bot.command('purchase', async (ctx) => {
  // 1. Mutate in memory
  ctx.session.balance -= 50;

  // 2. Outbound call fails
  await ctx.call('nonExistentMethod');

  // Invariant: Because this threw, ctx.session.balance remains 100!
});
```

---

## In-Process Mutex Serialization

When users rapidly double-tap inline buttons, multiple webhook updates arrive concurrently. Gramless serializes execution for the same user via `KeyedMutex`:

```text
User clicks button twice (rapid fire):
Update A ──────> [KeyedMutex: user:123] ───> Executes ───> Commits State
Update B ─────────────────── waiting ──────────────────> Reads Updated State ──> Commits
```

This completely eliminates lost read-modify-write updates.

---

## Important Scope Considerations

- **Scope of Rollback:** Transactional rollback applies strictly to staged session state (`ctx.session`). Outbound HTTP calls already delivered to Telegram (such as `await ctx.reply()`) are irrevocable network actions and cannot be undone if a downstream error occurs.
- **Concurrency Scope:** `KeyedMutex` serializes concurrent operations reaching the same V8 isolate process. In distributed environments where Telegram Serverless dispatches concurrent updates to separate parallel isolates, cross-isolate database coordination is handled at the SQLite storage layer.

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: guide/fsm.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Conversation Wizards (FSM)

Build multi-turn conversational forms, wizards, and state machines using `createFSM`.

---

## Step Declarations & Guards

```javascript
import { createBot, session, createFSM } from 'gramless';

export const bot = createBot();
bot.use(session());

const wizard = createFSM({
  cancelCommand: '/cancel',
  onCancel: async (ctx) => {
    await ctx.reply('Registration aborted.');
  },
});

// Step 1: Collect Name
wizard.step('ask_name', async (ctx) => {
  ctx.fsm.data.name = ctx.text.trim();
  await ctx.reply(`Hello ${ctx.fsm.data.name}! What is your email?`);
  ctx.fsm.goto('ask_email');
});

// Step 2: Collect Email with asynchronous validation guard
wizard.step(
  'ask_email',
  async (ctx) => {
    ctx.fsm.data.email = ctx.text.trim();
    ctx.fsm.complete();
    await ctx.reply(`Profile saved! Email: ${ctx.fsm.data.email}`);
  },
  // Validation guard: Rejects invalid emails and retains user on current step
  async (ctx) => {
    if (!ctx.text || !ctx.text.includes('@')) {
      await ctx.reply('Invalid email address. Please try again:');
      return false;
    }
    return true;
  }
);

bot.use(wizard.middleware());
```

---

## Navigation Controls

- `ctx.fsm.goto('stepName')`: Advance to a target scene.
- `ctx.fsm.back()`: Return to the previous step via the internal history stack.
- `ctx.fsm.complete()`: Wipe wizard state and conclude the conversation.
- `/cancel`: Built-in global abort command.

---

<!-- SECTION: guide/endpoints.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Mini App RPC Endpoints

Host serverless RPC functions in `tgcloud/endpoints/*.js` called directly by Telegram Mini Apps via `Telegram.WebApp.Serverless.call`.

---

## Defining Endpoints (`tgcloud/endpoints/submitScore.js`)

```javascript
import { createEndpoint, v } from 'gramless/endpoint';
import { db } from 'sdk';
import { leaderboard } from '../schema.js';

export default createEndpoint({
  requireAuth: true,
  schema: v.object({
    score: v.number({ min: 1, max: 1000000 }),
    tag: v.optional(v.string({ maxLength: 10 })),
  }),
}, async (ctx) => {
  const user = ctx.user; // Verified Telegram user from initData
  const { score } = ctx.input; // Validated payload

  await db.insert(leaderboard).values({
    tgId: user.id,
    firstName: user.first_name,
    score,
  }).run();

  return { success: true, rank: 1 };
});
```

---

## Schema Validator (`v`)

Gramless includes a sub-microsecond, zero-dependency schema validator:

- `v.string({ minLength, maxLength, pattern })`
- `v.number({ min, max })`
- `v.boolean()`
- `v.optional(schema)`
- `v.object({ [key]: schema })`
- `v.array(itemSchema)`

---

# AI Assistant & IDE Configuration

Configure AI coding assistants (Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Claude, ChatGPT) to write idiomatic, zero-dependency Gramless code without hallucinating third-party dependencies.

---

## 1. Standard Documentation Endpoints (`llms.txt`)

Gramless publishes machine-readable documentation compliant with the [`/llms.txt`](https://llmstxt.org) standard for AI models and search indexers:

| Resource | URL | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Index (`llms.txt`)** | `https://sidwiskers.github.io/gramless/llms.txt` | Clean markdown summary and structured directory of all guides, references, and recipes. |
| **Consolidated Docs (`llms-full.txt`)** | `https://sidwiskers.github.io/gramless/llms-full.txt` | Full concatenated documentation (52 KB) designed for direct context window ingestion. |

### Adding to Cursor or Windsurf Docs
In Cursor (`Settings > Features > Docs`) or Windsurf, add `https://sidwiskers.github.io/gramless/llms.txt` as a custom documentation source. The editor will automatically index Gramless APIs for contextual queries (`@docs`).

---

## 2. Cursor Configuration (`.cursorrules`)

Add a `.cursorrules` file to your project root to ensure Cursor completions adhere to Gramless conventions:

```markdown
# Gramless Development Guidelines

You are an expert Telegram Bot developer using Gramless (`gramless`).

## Rules & Constraints
- **Zero External Dependencies:** Do not import `axios`, `node-fetch`, `grammy`, or `telegraf`. Rely exclusively on `gramless`, native Web APIs (`fetch`, `crypto`), and Node.js built-ins.
- **Context Helpers:** Use `ctx.reply()`, `ctx.replyWithPhoto()`, and `ctx.replyWithKeyboard()` (the `chat_id` is inferred automatically).
- **Escape Hatch:** Use `await ctx.call(method, params)` for any Telegram Bot API method not covered by convenience helpers.
- **Callback Queries:** Always call `await ctx.answerCallbackQuery()` to dismiss client loading spinners.
- **Safe Formatting:** Always import `html`, `md`, or `fmt` from `gramless/format` when formatting messages with user variables to prevent injection attacks.
- **Offline Hermetic Testing:** Use `GramlessLab` from `gramless/testkit` with `node:test` for testing without network requests or bot tokens.
```

---

## 3. GitHub Copilot Configuration (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`)

GitHub Copilot and Copilot Workspace read instructions from `.github/copilot-instructions.md`:

```markdown
# GitHub Copilot Instructions

When generating code for Telegram bots in this repository:
- Use `gramless` for all routing, session management, and Bot API calls.
- Do not introduce external HTTP client or Telegram framework dependencies.
- In serverless handlers (TGCloud), export `bot.handler()`.
- In Cloudflare Workers, export `bot.fetch(request, env, ctx)`.
- In Node.js environments, use `bot.start()` for long polling.
- Write tests using `GramlessLab` from `gramless/testkit`.
```

---

## 4. Context Prompts for LLMs (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini)

When asking an LLM to generate or refactor a Gramless bot, provide the consolidated documentation link:

```text
Please write a Telegram bot using the Gramless framework. 
Documentation is available at: https://sidwiskers.github.io/gramless/llms-full.txt
Do not use any third-party dependencies.
```

<!-- SECTION: reference/context-api.md -->

# Context API Reference

Full method and property specification for `GramlessContext`.

---

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ctx.chatId` | `number \| string \| null` | Resolved identifier of the current chat |
| `ctx.userId` | `number \| null` | Resolved identifier of the user who triggered the update |
| `ctx.chatType` | `string \| null` | `'private'`, `'group'`, `'supergroup'`, or `'channel'` |
| `ctx.text` | `string \| null` | Incoming message text or empty string |
| `ctx.caption` | `string \| null` | Media caption or empty string |
| `ctx.data` | `string \| null` | Inline button callback payload or widget query data |
| `ctx.state` | `Record<string, any>` | Ephemeral update state for custom middlewares |
| `ctx.session` | `any` | Transactional persistent session data |
| `ctx.widgetQuery` | `WidgetQuery \| null` | Incoming widget interaction query (Bot API 10.4) |
| `ctx.sharedWidgetQuery` | `SharedWidgetQuery \| null` | Incoming shared widget query (Bot API 10.4) |
| `ctx.widget` | `Widget \| null` | HTML widget payload attached to a message |
| `ctx.tonWalletTransfer` | `TonWalletTransfer \| null` | TON blockchain transfer service message data |
| `ctx.paidMessagesWaived` | `PaidMessagesWaived \| null` | Waived paid messages count metadata |
| `ctx.elapsedMs` | `number` | Wall-clock milliseconds elapsed since update began |
| `ctx.deadline` | `number` | Unix timestamp of hard platform isolate execution deadline |

---

## Outbound Methods

### Message & Media
- `ctx.reply(text, options)`: Sends message to current chat. Supports `buttons: [...]` shorthand, `ephemeral: true`, and `quote_rich_texts: true`.
- `ctx.replyEphemeral(text, options)`: Sends an ephemeral message visible only to the active user; automatically omits `chat_id` and targets callback queries (Bot API 10.4).
- `ctx.replyWithHtml(html, options)`: Shorthand to send HTML formatted text.
- `ctx.replyWithMarkdown(markdown, options)`: Shorthand to send MarkdownV2 formatted text.
- `ctx.edit(text, options)`: Edits current message text.
- `ctx.editCaption(caption, options)`: Edits current message caption.
- `ctx.editKeyboard(keyboard)`: Edits current message reply markup.
- `ctx.sendPhoto(photo, options)`: Sends photo with optional caption.
- `ctx.sendVideo(video, options)`: Sends video.
- `ctx.sendVoice(voice, options)`: Sends voice note.
- `ctx.sendDocument(doc, options)`: Sends file document.
- `ctx.sendAnimation(animation, options)`: Sends animation/GIF.

### HTML Widgets (Bot API 10.4)
- `ctx.sendWidget(html, options)`: Sends private interactive HTML widget (1–32,768 bytes, auto-validated, protected from forwarding).
- `ctx.sendSharedWidget(widgetId, options)`: Re-sends a shared widget created by the bot.
- `ctx.answerWidgetQuery(data, options)`: Responds to an incoming query sent from an HTML widget.
- `ctx.editMessageWidgetData(options)`: Updates binary data of a widget attached to a message.
- `ctx.editSharedWidgetData(widgetId, publicData, options)`: Updates global public state data of a shared widget with caching.

### Unique Gifts & Themes (Bot API 10.4)
- `ctx.getUniqueGift(name)`: Retrieves unique gift model by name.
- `ctx.deleteBusinessAccountGift(businessConnectionId, ownedGiftId)`: Removes a gift from a connected business account.
- `ctx.getChatShareThemeBackdrops()`: Retrieves available theme backdrops for chat sharing.

### Interactivity & Reactions
- `ctx.react(emoji)`: Adds a native emoji reaction to the message.
- `ctx.chatAction(action)`: Broadcasts action (e.g. `'typing'`, `'upload_photo'`).
- `ctx.answer(text, options)`: Dismisses callback query loading indicator.
- `ctx.alert(text)`: Displays an alert modal toast for callback queries.

### Moderation & Administration
- `ctx.banMember(userId, options)`: Bans a user from the chat.
- `ctx.unbanMember(userId)`: Unbans a user.
- `ctx.banSender(revokeMessages)`: Bans author of current message and optionally deletes their messages.
- `ctx.restrictMember(userId, options)`: Restricts chat member permissions.
- `ctx.delete()`: Deletes current message.
- `ctx.pin(options)` / `ctx.unpin()`: Pins or unpins current message.

### Execution Clock & Checkpointing
- `ctx.remainingMs()`: Returns milliseconds remaining before hard isolate execution deadline.
- `ctx.hasTimeFor(bufferMs)`: Returns `true` if remaining budget exceeds `bufferMs`.
- `await ctx.checkpoint()`: Immediately commits intermediate session state to SQLite before isolate timeout.

### Direct Method Invocation
- `ctx.call(method, params)`: Calls any Telegram Bot API method directly.

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: reference/filter-api.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Filter API Reference

API specifications for functional filters exported from `gramless/filters` or root `Filter`.

---

## Combinators

### `Filter.all(...predicates)`
Returns a predicate that passes if and only if **all** provided sub-predicates evaluate to `true`. Short-circuits on first `false`.

### `Filter.any(...predicates)`
Returns a predicate that passes if **any** provided sub-predicate evaluates to `true`. Short-circuits on first `true`.

### `Filter.not(predicate)`
Returns a predicate that negates the result of the provided predicate.

---

## Content Filters

- `Filter.hasText` (`Filter.text`): Passes if update contains non-empty text.
- `Filter.hasPhoto` (`Filter.photo`): Passes if update contains photo attachments.
- `Filter.hasVideo` (`Filter.video`): Passes if update contains video attachments.
- `Filter.hasVoice` (`Filter.voice`): Passes if update contains voice notes.
- `Filter.hasAudio` (`Filter.audio`): Passes if update contains audio files.
- `Filter.hasDocument` (`Filter.document`): Passes if update contains document files.
- `Filter.hasSticker` (`Filter.sticker`): Passes if update contains stickers.
- `Filter.hasAnimation` (`Filter.animation`): Passes if update contains animations/GIFs.
- `Filter.hasLocation` (`Filter.location`): Passes if update contains location coordinates.
- `Filter.hasContact` (`Filter.contact`): Passes if update contains contacts.
- `Filter.hasPoll` (`Filter.poll`): Passes if update contains a poll.
- `Filter.hasDice` (`Filter.dice`): Passes if update contains animated dice.

---

## Bot API 10.4 Filters

- `Filter.hasWidget` (`Filter.widget`): Passes if the message contains an attached HTML widget.
- `Filter.isWidgetQuery` (`Filter.widgetQuery`): Passes if update is an incoming query from an HTML widget.
- `Filter.isSharedWidgetQuery` (`Filter.sharedWidgetQuery`): Passes if update is an incoming query from a shared HTML widget.
- `Filter.hasTonTransfer` (`Filter.tonTransfer`): Passes if update is a TON blockchain transfer service message.
- `Filter.hasPaidMessagesWaived` (`Filter.paidMessagesWaived`): Passes if update is a paid messages waived service notification.

---

## Chat Type Filters

- `Filter.private`: Passes if message is from a 1-on-1 private chat.
- `Filter.group`: Passes if chat type is `'group'` or `'supergroup'`.
- `Filter.channel`: Passes if chat type is `'channel'`.

---

## Parameterized Filters

- `Filter.textPrefix(prefix)`: Matches messages starting with a specific prefix string.
- `Filter.textMatches(regex)`: Matches messages satisfying a regular expression.
- `Filter.fromUsers(...userIds)`: Matches updates from specified user IDs.
- `Filter.inChats(...chatIds)`: Matches updates originating in specified chat IDs.

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: reference/testkit.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Gramless Lab (Testkit Reference)

API specification for deterministic, offline testing via `gramless/testkit`.

---

## `createLab(bot)`
Creates a virtual in-process Telegram testing harness.

```javascript
import { createLab } from 'gramless/testkit';
import { bot } from './bot.js';

const lab = createLab(bot);
```

---

## `lab.user(id, [firstName])`
Creates a virtual user actor.

### Actor Simulation Methods
- `await actor.command(commandText)`: Simulates sending a command (e.g. `'/start'`).
- `await actor.message(text, [options])`: Simulates sending standard message text.
- `await actor.click(callbackData)`: Simulates clicking an inline keyboard button.
- `await actor.inline(query, [offset])`: Simulates an inline search query.
- `await actor.queryWidget(data, [options])`: Simulates an incoming query from an HTML widget (Bot API 10.4).
- `await actor.querySharedWidget(widgetId, data, [options])`: Simulates an incoming query from a shared HTML widget (Bot API 10.4).

---

## Fluent Matchers

Actor action results return a chainable `ActorExpectation`:

- `res.wantSent(pattern, [options])`: Asserts that a message matching string or regex pattern was sent.
- `res.wantEdited(pattern)`: Asserts that an existing message was edited with matching text.
- `res.wantAnswered([pattern])`: Asserts that `answerCallbackQuery` was called.
- `res.wantWidgetSent([pattern])`: Asserts that an HTML widget message was sent (`sendWidget` or `sendSharedWidget`).
- `res.wantWidgetQueryAnswered([dataPattern])`: Asserts that `answerWidgetQuery` was called with matching data.
- `res.wantInlineAnswered([expectedCount])`: Asserts that `answerInlineQuery` was called.
- `res.want(matcherFn)`: Custom assertion matcher function `(calls) => void`.

```javascript
const res = await alice.command('/menu');
res.wantSent('Main Menu:');

const widgetRes = await alice.queryWidget('action:vote:a');
widgetRes.wantWidgetQueryAnswered('voted');
```

---

<!-- SECTION: reference/benchmarks.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Performance & Scale Benchmarks

Reproducible benchmark metrics measured across 10,000 iterations per scenario using Node's high-resolution performance timers (`performance.now()` / `process.hrtime.bigint()`).

---

## Benchmark Results (ARM64 / Node v22)

| Scenario | Complexity / Scale | Latency (µs / op) | Throughput (ops / sec) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Exact Action Dispatch** | 500 registered callback routes | **0.92 µs** | **1,087,209** |
| **Exact Command Dispatch** | 1,000 registered routes | **2.25 µs** | **444,131** |
| **Schema Validation (`v`)** | Multi-field object + nested constraints | **0.49 µs** | **2,023,848** |
| **Safe HTML Template (`html`)** | Tagged template literal interpolation | **1.74 µs** | **573,865** |
| **Middleware Pipeline** | 10 onion layers + route execution | **7.01 µs** | **142,666** |

---

## Architecture Comparison

| Metric | Traditional Frameworks | Gramless |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Dependencies** | 15–40 packages | **0 packages** |
| **Cold-Start Time** | 40ms – 180ms | **< 3ms** |
| **Package Size** | ~1.5 MB – 5.0 MB | **~53 KB (tarball) / ~209 KB (unpacked)** |
| **Session Isolation** | In-memory cache or async uncoordinated DB writes | **ACID SQLite with automatic rollback** |
| **Routing Algorithm** | Linear $O(N)$ middleware arrays | **$O(1)$ Hash Map & Prefix Index** |

---

## How to Reproduce

Clone the repository and run:

```bash
npm run bench
```

<!-- SECTION: cookbook/01-minimal-bot.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Recipe 01: Minimal Bot

A minimal, production-ready bot demonstrating the recommended TGCloud directory architecture and single-line handler exports with **Gramless**.

---

## Architecture & Mental Model

In Telegram Serverless (TGCloud), incoming updates are dispatched to individual files in `tgcloud/handlers/` depending on the update type:
- `tgcloud/handlers/message.js` receives `message` updates.
- `tgcloud/handlers/callback_query.js` receives inline button clicks.

Instead of writing separate, uncoordinated routing logic in each handler file, the idiomatic Gramless architecture is:
1. Define all commands, actions, and middlewares once on a shared bot instance in `tgcloud/lib/bot.js`.
2. Re-export `bot.handler()` from each handler file.

```text
01-minimal-bot/
├── tgcloud/
│   ├── handlers/
│   │   ├── message.js          # export default bot.handler();
│   │   └── callback_query.js   # export default bot.handler();
│   └── lib/
│       └── bot.js              # Centralized route definitions
├── package.json
└── tgcloud.jsonc
```

When TGCloud routes an update into `message.js` or `callback_query.js`, `bot.handler()` automatically extracts the payload, matches the registered route in constant time ($O(1)$), and runs the callback.

---

## Code Walkthrough

### 1. Route Definitions (`tgcloud/lib/bot.js`)

```javascript
import { createBot } from 'gramless';

export const bot = createBot();

bot.command('start', async (ctx) => {
  await ctx.chatAction('typing');

  await ctx.reply(`Welcome <b>${ctx.from?.first_name || 'User'}</b>!`, {
    parse_mode: 'HTML',
    buttons: [
      [{ text: 'Ping isolate', data: 'action:ping' }],
      [{ text: 'Official documentation', url: 'https://github.com/sidwiskers/gramless' }],
    ],
  });
});

bot.action('action:ping', async (ctx) => {
  await ctx.answer({ text: 'Pong received' });
  await ctx.edit(`<b>Pong</b>\n\nButton callback executed at <code>${new Date().toISOString()}</code>`, {
    parse_mode: 'HTML',
    buttons: [
      [{ text: 'Refresh', data: 'action:ping' }],
    ],
  });
});
```

### 2. Handler Re-exports (`tgcloud/handlers/message.js`)

```javascript
import { bot } from '../lib/bot.js';

export default bot.handler();
```

---

## Deployment to TGCloud

Ensure you have `@tgcloud/cli` installed and authenticated:

```bash
# Verify local diff against cloud
tgcloud diff

# Push code and activate bot
tgcloud push
```

---

## Key Considerations

- **Relative Imports Must Include Extensions:** In TGCloud V8 isolates, `import { bot } from '../lib/bot'` fails. You must specify the `.js` extension: `import { bot } from '../lib/bot.js'`.
- **Answering Callbacks:** Always call `await ctx.answer()` inside `bot.action()` handlers to dismiss the loading spinner on Telegram clients.

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: cookbook/02-database-crud.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Recipe 02: Transactional SQLite CRUD & Persistence

This recipe shows how to build a persistent Task Manager bot using Telegram Serverless's native SQLite engine (`sdk/db`) combined with Gramless's transactional session middleware.

---

## State Consistency & Transactional Sessions

In serverless execution environments, incoming updates trigger separate V8 isolate invocations:
1. **Uncoordinated Database Writes:** Traditional state stores commit mutations immediately. If an outbound Telegram API call fails halfway through (e.g., due to network interruptions or invalid parameters), external databases can be left in an inconsistent state.
2. **Foreign Key Support:** TGCloud SQLite operates with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF`. Declaring `.references()` is not supported and throws an error at startup.

### Gramless State Handling
- **Transactional Rollback:** When using `bot.use(session({ store: new TgCloudSessionStore(...) }))`, mutations to `ctx.session` are held in an in-memory staging copy. Only when the handler resolves successfully are changes committed to the SQLite database. If an unhandled error occurs, staged mutations are discarded.
- **Mutex Serialization:** Rapid sequential updates from the same user are serialized through `KeyedMutex` to prevent concurrent read-modify-write conflicts.

---

## Directory Structure

```text
02-database-crud/
├── tgcloud/
│   ├── schema.js               # Declarative SQLite tables & indexes
│   ├── handlers/
│   │   ├── message.js          # export default bot.handler();
│   │   └── callback_query.js   # export default bot.handler();
│   └── lib/
│       └── bot.js              # Bot routes & CRUD operations
├── package.json
└── tgcloud.jsonc
```

---

## Schema Declaration (`tgcloud/schema.js`)

All tables must be declared using the `sdk/db` DSL:

```javascript
import { table, integer, text, boolean, json, index, sql } from 'sdk/db';

export const tasks = table('tasks', {
  id:          integer('id').primaryKey({ autoIncrement: true }),
  userId:      integer('user_id').notNull(),
  title:       text('title').notNull(),
  isCompleted: boolean('is_completed').default(false),
  createdAt:   integer('created_at', { mode: 'timestamp' }).default(sql`(unixepoch())`),
}, (t) => ({
  userStatusIdx: index('idx_tasks_user_status').on(t.userId, t.isCompleted),
}));

export const sessions = table('sessions', {
  id:        text('id').primaryKey(),
  data:      json('data'),
  updatedAt: integer('updated_at', { mode: 'timestamp' }).default(sql`(unixepoch())`),
});
```

---

## Deploying Schema & Handlers

When deploying with `@tgcloud/cli`:
1. Use `tgcloud diff` to inspect pending schema and code changes.
2. Run `tgcloud migrate` to apply any pending SQLite DDL migrations defined in `tgcloud/schema.js`.
3. Run `tgcloud push` to upload code and activate your handlers.

```bash
# Preview schema migrations and code diff
tgcloud diff

# Apply SQLite schema migrations
tgcloud migrate

# Deploy code and static assets
tgcloud push
```

---

## Key Considerations

- **Asynchronous DB Operations:** In `sdk/db`, database queries return Promises. Always `await` query execution (`await db.select().from(table)...`).
- **Foreign Keys:** Avoid declaring `.references()`. Instead, store related identifiers as integer columns (e.g. `integer('user_id').notNull()`) and filter with query predicates such as `eq(tasks.userId, ctx.userId)`.

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: cookbook/03-onboarding-wizard.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Recipe 03: Multi-Step Conversation Wizards (FSM)

This recipe demonstrates building conversational forms and multi-turn onboarding flows using **Gramless FSM** (`createFSM`).

---

## Multi-Turn Conversations in Serverless Runtimes

In a serverless architecture, each incoming update arrives in an independent execution context. Managing multi-step interactions requires maintaining conversational state between requests:
- Tracking user progression across multiple messages.
- Validating intermediate input before moving to the next step.
- Handling branching, cancellation (`/cancel`), or step rewinding (`/back`).

### Finite State Machine Implementation
Gramless includes an integrated FSM engine (`createFSM`) that coordinates directly with your session store:
- **`wizard.step(name, handler, [guard])`**: Defines a conversation step with an optional validation guard. If the guard returns `false`, execution stops and the user remains on the current step.
- **`ctx.fsm.goto(nextStep)`**: Transitions the conversation to a designated step.
- **`ctx.fsm.back()`**: Returns to the previous step using an internal transition stack.
- **`ctx.fsm.complete()`**: Completes the conversation and clears wizard state.
- **`cancelCommand: '/cancel'`**: Global cancellation command that resets conversation state.

---

## Directory Structure

```text
03-onboarding-wizard/
├── tgcloud/
│   ├── handlers/
│   │   └── message.js          # export default bot.handler();
│   └── lib/
│       └── bot.js              # FSM scenes and routes
├── package.json
└── tgcloud.jsonc
```

---

## Code Walkthrough

```javascript
import { createBot, session, createFSM } from 'gramless';

export const bot = createBot();
bot.use(session());

const wizard = createFSM({
  cancelCommand: '/cancel',
  onCancel: async (ctx) => {
    await ctx.reply('Wizard cancelled.');
  },
});

// Step 1: Input text with string length guard
wizard.step('ask_name', async (ctx) => {
  ctx.fsm.data.name = ctx.text.trim();
  await ctx.reply(`Hello ${ctx.fsm.data.name}. What is your age?`);
  ctx.fsm.goto('ask_age');
}, async (ctx) => {
  if (!ctx.text || ctx.text.trim().length < 2) {
    await ctx.reply('Please provide a valid name (at least 2 characters):');
    return false; // Rejects update, keeps user on 'ask_name'
  }
  return true;
});

// Attach FSM middleware to bot
bot.use(wizard.middleware());
```

---

## Key Considerations

- **Session Middleware Must Precede FSM:** `bot.use(session(...))` must be registered **before** `bot.use(wizard.middleware())`, as the FSM stores scene state and transition history directly inside `ctx.session.__fsm`.
- **Always Await Guard Predicates:** Guards can be asynchronous (e.g. querying a database to verify an invite code). Ensure you return a boolean `true` or `false`.

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: cookbook/04-mini-app-rpc.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Recipe 04: Fullstack Mini App RPC & WebApp Integration

This recipe shows how to build an end-to-end Telegram Mini App where a client-side frontend calls serverless backend endpoints via `Telegram.WebApp.Serverless.call`, verified and validated using **Gramless Endpoint** (`createEndpoint`).

---

## Overview: Mini App Architecture & Authentication

Building Telegram Mini Apps with serverless backends involves:
1. Serving static assets (HTML/CSS/JS) securely via CDN.
2. Authenticating incoming client requests by validating Telegram `initData`.
3. Validating payload structures before passing them to database and business logic.

### Gramless & TGCloud Integration
- **Static Hosting:** Setting `"static": "public"` in `tgcloud.jsonc` serves frontend assets directly from Telegram's CDN with HTTPS enabled.
- **Caller Identity:** TGCloud validates caller signatures before invoking your isolate. Setting `createEndpoint({ requireAuth: true })` ensures that only authenticated requests reach the handler, attaching verified user data to `ctx.user`.
- **Schema Validation:** Gramless includes lightweight schema validators (`v.string()`, `v.number()`, `v.boolean()`, `v.object()`) for runtime payload validation without external dependencies.

---

## Directory Structure

```text
04-mini-app-rpc/
├── public/                     # Static files served on Telegram CDN
│   ├── index.html
│   └── app.js                  # Frontend calling Telegram.WebApp.Serverless.call
├── tgcloud/
│   ├── schema.js               # SQLite leaderboard table
│   ├── endpoints/              # Flat directory of RPC endpoints
│   │   ├── getLeaderboard.js
│   │   └── submitScore.js
│   └── handlers/
│       └── message.js          # Bot command to launch Mini App
├── package.json
└── tgcloud.jsonc
```

---

## Backend Endpoint Definition (`tgcloud/endpoints/submitScore.js`)

```javascript
import { createEndpoint, v } from 'gramless/endpoint';
import { db } from 'sdk';
import { sql } from 'sdk/db';
import { leaderboard } from '../schema.js';

export default createEndpoint({
  requireAuth: true,
  schema: v.object({
    score: v.number({ min: 1, max: 1000000 }),
  }),
}, async (ctx) => {
  const user = ctx.user; // Verified Telegram user
  const { score } = ctx.input; // Guaranteed valid number

  await db.insert(leaderboard).values({
    tgId: user.id,
    firstName: user.first_name,
    score,
  }).run();

  return { success: true, score };
});
```

---

## Frontend Invocation (`public/app.js`)

```javascript
// Invoking serverless RPC from the Mini App via callback
Telegram.WebApp.Serverless.call('submitScore', { score: 1500 }, (err, result) => {
  if (err) {
    console.error('Call failed:', err);
    return;
  }
  console.log('Server response:', result);
});

// Or using an asynchronous Promise wrapper:
const callEndpoint = (name, payload) =>
  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    Telegram.WebApp.Serverless.call(name, payload, (err, res) => {
      if (err) reject(err);
      else resolve(res);
    });
  });

const result = await callEndpoint('submitScore', { score: 1500 });
console.log('Server response:', result);
```

---

## Key Considerations

- **Flat Endpoint Hierarchy:** Endpoint files must reside directly in `tgcloud/endpoints/` (e.g. `tgcloud/endpoints/submitScore.js`). Nested subdirectories inside `endpoints/` are not supported.
- **Verified Caller Identity:** In the raw platform context, verified user information is located at `ctx.initData.user`. Gramless provides access directly on `ctx.user`.

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: cookbook/05-telegram-stars.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Recipe 05: Telegram Stars Paywall & Digital Goods

This recipe shows how to monetize your Telegram bot using native **Telegram Stars** (`currency: 'XTR'`), handle the two-phase checkout lifecycle, and persist purchase confirmations to SQLite.

---

## The Two-Phase Checkout Lifecycle

Telegram's native digital goods payment system requires a strict two-phase handshake:
1. **Invoice Issuance:** The bot sends an invoice message with `currency: 'XTR'` (the official ISO symbol for Telegram Stars).
2. **Pre-Checkout Handshake (`pre_checkout_query`):** When the user clicks "Pay", Telegram's payment servers ping your webhook with a `pre_checkout_query`. Your bot **must respond within 10 seconds** via `answerPreCheckoutQuery(true)` to approve the charge, or `answerPreCheckoutQuery(false, { error_message })` to reject it (e.g. if the item is out of stock).
3. **Fulfillment (`successful_payment`):** Once payment settles, Telegram sends a `message` containing `successful_payment`. You must save `telegram_payment_charge_id` to prevent duplicate fulfillments.

---

## Directory Structure

```text
05-telegram-stars/
├── tgcloud/
│   ├── schema.js                  # Purchases table
│   ├── handlers/
│   │   ├── message.js             # Invoices & successful_payment fulfillment
│   │   └── pre_checkout_query.js  # Approves/rejects transaction handshake
│   └── lib/
│       └── bot.js                 # Shared payment routing logic
├── package.json
└── tgcloud.jsonc
```

---

## Code Walkthrough

### 1. Issuing a Telegram Stars Invoice

```javascript
bot.command('buy', async (ctx) => {
  await ctx.sendInvoice({
    title: 'VIP Community Membership',
    description: 'Instant 30-day access to premium analytics.',
    payload: `vip_membership_${ctx.userId}_${Date.now()}`,
    currency: 'XTR', // Telegram Stars currency code
    prices: [
      { label: 'VIP Pass', amount: 50 }, // 50 Stars
    ],
  });
});
```

### 2. Pre-Checkout Verification

```javascript
bot.on('pre_checkout_query', async (ctx) => {
  const query = ctx.raw.pre_checkout_query || ctx.raw;
  
  // Verify order payload or inventory
  if (!query.invoice_payload?.startsWith('vip_membership_')) {
    return ctx.answerPreCheckoutQuery(false, {
      error_message: 'This product is no longer active.',
    });
  }

  // Authorize Telegram to charge user
  await ctx.answerPreCheckoutQuery(true);
});
```

### 3. Fulfilling the Order

```javascript
bot.on('successful_payment', async (ctx) => {
  const payment = ctx.raw.successful_payment || ctx.raw.message?.successful_payment;

  await db.insert(purchases).values({
    userId: ctx.userId,
    item: 'vip_membership',
    starsPaid: payment.total_amount,
    telegramPaymentChargeId: payment.telegram_payment_charge_id,
  }).run();

  await ctx.reply(`Payment confirmed. VIP pass is activated.`);
});
```

---

## Key Considerations

- **Provider Token is Empty for Stars:** For traditional credit cards or Stripe payments, Telegram requires a payment provider token. For **Telegram Stars**, leave `provider_token` empty or omitted—Telegram processes Stars natively.
- **Dedicated Handler for `pre_checkout_query`:** In TGCloud, `pre_checkout_query` updates are routed directly to `tgcloud/handlers/pre_checkout_query.js`. Failing to export a handler for this file will cause checkout attempts to time out.

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: cookbook/06-group-moderation.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Recipe 06: Group and Channel Moderation

This recipe demonstrates anti-spam link filtering and administrator moderation tools using **Gramless Composable Filters** (`Filter`).

---

## High-Volume Group Updates & Filtering

Group chats can generate a significant volume of messages and events. Handling these updates efficiently requires:
- Filtering out irrelevant chat types and message payloads early in the execution pipeline.
- Avoiding redundant regex compilations or unnecessary database queries.
- Providing direct access to Telegram chat administration methods.

### Composable Filter Architecture
- **Composable Filters:** Gramless provides functional filter combinators (`Filter.all`, `Filter.any`, `Filter.not`) that short-circuit immediately if conditions fail.
- **Context Administration Helpers:** Context exposes moderation helpers (`ctx.banSender(true)`, `ctx.restrictMember()`, `ctx.delete()`, `ctx.unbanMember()`) that automatically infer the current `chat_id` and `message_id`.

---

## Directory Structure

```text
06-group-moderation/
├── tgcloud/
│   ├── handlers/
│   │   ├── message.js          # Spam detection & moderation commands
│   │   └── my_chat_member.js   # Bot rights status tracking
│   └── lib/
│       └── bot.js              # Composable filter routing
├── package.json
└── tgcloud.jsonc
```

---

## Code Walkthrough

### 1. Declarative Spam Filtering

```javascript
import { createBot, Filter } from 'gramless';

export const bot = createBot();

const hasSpamLink = (ctx) => {
  const text = ctx.text || ctx.caption || '';
  return /(?:https?:\/\/)?t\.me\/[a-zA-Z0-9_]{5,}/i.test(text);
};

// Composes: MUST be a group AND MUST contain a spam link
bot.on(Filter.all(Filter.group, hasSpamLink), async (ctx) => {
  // Delete the spam message immediately
  await ctx.delete();

  // Mute author for 1 hour
  const until = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600;
  await ctx.restrictMember(ctx.userId, {
    permissions: { can_send_messages: false },
    until_date: until,
  });
});
```

### 2. Administrator Moderation Commands

```javascript
bot.command('ban', async (ctx) => {
  const target = ctx.message?.reply_to_message?.from;
  if (!target) return ctx.reply('Reply to the message of the user to ban.');

  // Bans the user and revokes all their past messages from the chat
  await ctx.banMember(target.id, { revoke_messages: true });
  await ctx.reply(`Banned ${target.first_name}.`);
});
```

---

## Key Considerations

- **Bot Must Have Admin Rights:** Moderation methods (`deleteMessage`, `banChatMember`, `restrictChatMember`) require appropriate administrator privileges in the group. If permissions are missing, Telegram returns a `400 Bad Request: NOT_ENOUGH_RIGHTS`.
- **Bot Updates on Group Status:** When users add the bot to a group or change its administrator rights, Telegram delivers a `my_chat_member` update, NOT a `message`. Handle it in `tgcloud/handlers/my_chat_member.js`.

---


<!-- ========================================== -->
<!-- SECTION: cookbook/07-lab-testing.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Recipe 07: Hermetic Testing with Gramless Lab

This recipe demonstrates how to write 100% deterministic, offline automated tests for your Telegram bots using **Gramless Lab** (`gramless/testkit`) and Node's built-in test runner (`node:test`).

---

## Testing Strategy & Challenges

Testing Telegram bots often presents logistical challenges:
1. Managing dedicated test bot tokens via @BotFather.
2. Executing live HTTP requests to `api.telegram.org` during CI pipelines, introducing network latency and rate limits.
3. Maintaining mock HTTP fixtures that can drift from Telegram Bot API specifications.

### The Gramless Lab Approach
Gramless Lab (`gramless/testkit`) executes tests completely in-process:
- **Offline Mock Engine:** Outbound API calls (`sendMessage`, `editMessageText`, `answerCallbackQuery`) are intercepted by an in-memory client.
- **Virtual User Actors:** Multi-turn interactions are simulated using `lab.user(id, name)`.
- **Declarative Assertions:** Response expectations are verified using `Sent('pattern')`, `Edited('pattern')`, and `Answered()`.
- **Session Isolation:** Each virtual actor maintains independent session state, enabling deterministic concurrency testing.

---

## Directory Structure

```text
07-lab-testing/
├── bot.js                      # The bot under test
├── tests/
│   └── bot.test.js             # Gramless Lab offline test suite
└── package.json                # "scripts": { "test": "node --test tests/*.test.js" }
```

---

## Code Walkthrough

### 1. The Bot Implementation (`bot.js`)

```javascript
import { createBot, session } from 'gramless';

export function createTestBot() {
  const bot = createBot();

  bot.use(session({ initial: () => ({ counter: 0 }) }));

  bot.command('start', async (ctx) => {
    await ctx.reply(`Welcome ${ctx.from?.first_name}!`, {
      buttons: [[{ text: '+1 Increment', data: 'action:inc' }]],
    });
  });

  bot.action('action:inc', async (ctx) => {
    ctx.session.counter += 1;
    await ctx.answer('Incremented!');
    await ctx.edit(`Current count: ${ctx.session.counter}`);
  });

  return bot;
}
```

### 2. The Offline Test Suite (`tests/bot.test.js`)

```javascript
import test from 'node:test';
import { createLab, Sent, Edited, Answered } from 'gramless/testkit';
import { createTestBot } from '../bot.js';

test('Simulate multi-turn user conversation offline', async () => {
  const bot = createTestBot();
  const lab = createLab(bot);
  const alice = lab.user(101, 'Alice');

  // 1. Alice sends /start command
  const res1 = await alice.command('/start');
  res1.want(Sent('Welcome Alice!'));

  // 2. Alice clicks the "+1 Increment" inline button
  const res2 = await alice.click('action:inc');
  res2.want(Answered('Incremented!'));
  res2.want(Edited('Current count: 1'));

  // 3. Alice clicks again — verifies session persistence
  const res3 = await alice.click('action:inc');
  res3.want(Edited('Current count: 2'));
});
```

---

## Running the Tests

Run directly using Node.js's built-in test runner without installing Jest, Mocha, or Vitest:

```bash
npm test
```

---

<!-- SECTION: cookbook/08-migration-guide.md -->
<!-- ========================================== -->

# Recipe 08: Migration Guide (grammY & Telegraf to Gramless)

This guide provides a comprehensive, side-by-side technical translation for developers migrating existing bots from **grammY** or **Telegraf** to **Gramless** on **Telegram Serverless (TGCloud)**.

---

## 1. Core Mental Model Shift

Traditional Node.js frameworks were designed for long-running servers. TGCloud runs discrete V8 isolates on Telegram's edge:

| Feature / Architecture | grammY / Telegraf | Gramless (TGCloud) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Execution Model** | Persistent Node.js process | Ephemeral V8 isolates |
| **Bot Token Handling** | Read via `process.env.BOT_TOKEN` | Managed by Telegram Cloud proxy (no tokens in code) |
| **Ingress Pipeline** | `bot.start()` (long polling) or Express webhook | `export default bot.handler()` |
| **Runtime Dependencies** | External packages | **Zero external dependencies** |
| **Database & Sessions** | External Redis / MongoDB / Postgres | Built-in SQLite (`sdk/db`) with transactional rollback |
| **Mini App Backend** | External Express / FastAPI backend | Built-in serverless RPC (`createEndpoint`) |

---

## 2. Side-by-Side Syntax Translation

### Initialization & Entry Point

#### In grammY / Telegraf:
```javascript
// Requires token and long-polling loop or webhook server
import { Bot } from 'grammy'; // or { Telegraf } from 'telegraf';

const bot = new Bot(process.env.BOT_TOKEN);

bot.command('start', (ctx) => ctx.reply('Hello!'));

bot.start(); // Blocks process
```

#### In Gramless (TGCloud):
```javascript
// Zero tokens required in TGCloud, instant export
import { createBot } from 'gramless';

export const bot = createBot();

bot.command('start', async (ctx) => {
  await ctx.reply('Hello!');
});

// Single-line handler export for TGCloud:
export default bot.handler();
```

---

### Keyboards & Inline Markups

#### In grammY / Telegraf:
```javascript
// Requires importing keyboard builder class
import { InlineKeyboard } from 'grammy';

const keyboard = new InlineKeyboard()
  .text('Click me', 'btn_click')
  .row()
  .url('Website', 'https://example.com');

await ctx.reply('Menu:', { reply_markup: keyboard });
```

#### In Gramless:
```javascript
// Array shorthand without extra imports
await ctx.reply('Menu:', {
  buttons: [
    [{ text: 'Click me', data: 'btn_click' }],
    [{ text: 'Website', url: 'https://example.com' }],
  ],
});
```

---

### Sessions & State Management

#### In grammY / Telegraf:
```javascript
// External Redis adapter
import { session } from 'grammy';
import { RedisAdapter } from '@grammyjs/storage-redis';

bot.use(session({
  storage: new RedisAdapter({ instance: redisClient }),
}));

bot.command('transfer', async (ctx) => {
  ctx.session.balance -= 50;
  await callExternalPayment(); // If this fails, state is already updated
});
```

#### In Gramless:
```javascript
// SQLite session store with transactional staging
import { session, TgCloudSessionStore } from 'gramless';
import { db } from 'sdk';
import { eq } from 'sdk/db';
import { sessions } from '../schema.js';

bot.use(session({
  store: new TgCloudSessionStore({ db, table: sessions, eq }),
  initial: () => ({ balance: 100 }),
}));

bot.command('transfer', async (ctx) => {
  ctx.session.balance -= 50;
  await callExternalPayment(); // If this throws, ctx.session rolls back automatically
});
```

---

### Composable Filters

#### In grammY:
```javascript
// grammY filter queries
bot.on('message:photo', async (ctx) => { ... });
bot.filter((ctx) => ctx.chat?.type === 'group', async (ctx) => { ... });
```

#### In Gramless:
```javascript
// Functional filter combinators
import { Filter } from 'gramless';

// Matches photos inside groups:
bot.on(Filter.all(Filter.group, Filter.hasPhoto), async (ctx) => {
  await ctx.reply('Photo received.');
});
```

---

## 3. Common Migration Considerations

1. **Deploying on TGCloud vs Traditional Servers:** In TGCloud, export `bot.handler()`. When running on traditional servers (VPS or container), use `bot.start()` for polling or `bot.webhookCallback()` for HTTP servers.
2. **ES Module Imports:** TGCloud V8 isolates enforce standard ECMAScript module resolution. Relative imports must include file extensions (`import { bot } from './lib/bot.js'`).
3. **Asynchronous Database Calls:** In `sdk/db`, all query builder operations are asynchronous and return Promises. Always prefix queries with `await`.
4. **Token Management on TGCloud:** In TGCloud environments, the API client communicates automatically via the runtime proxy (`import { api } from 'sdk'`). Bot tokens do not need to be passed in application code.

---
